result.summary: Independent Phase 2A security review approved. All 21 tests pass. PKCE with S256, CSRF protection, tenant isolation, and audit logging verified. No critical defects. Username collision retracted: authentication resolves by immutable subject_id, not login. Operational considerations: GitHub username reassignment may cause login ambiguity but no auth impact. Standard bearer token risk documented. Edge rate limiting recommended for production.
result.details: Security review of commit 6ef4bc0 (HEAD) against base cda607e. OAuth 2.0/PKCE implementation verified with fixed HTTPS endpoints, confidential code exchange via AES-GCM sealed verifier, browser-bound state tokens, and read:user scope. Session security includes SHA-256 hashed tokens, HttpOnly/Secure cookies, 12h TTL, revocation, and disabled account blocking. CSRF protected via HMAC-signed tokens bound to session and validated origins. Tenant isolation enforced via membership JOINs with active status checks. Cursor pagination signed and bound to subject/scope/purpose. Idempotency includes live authorization recheck. Audit logging covers all account/session/membership events. Retraction: Previous claim that username collision grants dual identities is incorrect. Evidence: authentication resolves by immutable provider+subject_id (apps/cloud/src/provider.ts:19), users/external_identities have unique subject_id constraint (migrations/0001_identity.sql:7-12), test verifies repeated login with username change retains same subject_id (test/auth.integration.ts:178-198). Operational considerations: (1) GitHub username reassignment may cause login field collisions but authentication remains secure, (2) standard bearer token risk applies (documented), (3) no in-code rate limiting on auth endpoints.

tests.summary: 21 tests passed, 0 failed. Verified PKCE login with real Miniflare D1 integration, callback replay protection, identity immutability, concurrent sign-in, expired state rejection, provider failure handling, cross-tenant isolation, cursor binding, session/revocation handling, CSRF validation, audit rollback, and idempotency.
